target: À peine fut-il sorti qu'il se mit à pleuvoir.
english: He had barely gone out when it started to rain.
tip: 'À peine fut-il sorti que' = 'barely had he left when.' Fronting à peine flips subject and verb (fut-il), just like the English inversion.

target: C'est là que le bât blesse.
english: That's where the shoe pinches.
tip: 'Le bât blesse' = 'the packsaddle hurts'. Where the problem lies.

target: C'est ce en quoi je crois fermement.
english: That's what I firmly believe in.
tip: 'Ce en quoi': preposition + quoi after 'croire en'.

target: Ils vécurent heureux et eurent beaucoup d'enfants.
english: They lived happily and had many children.
tip: Classic fairy tale ending. Passé simple of vivre: vécurent.

target: Aussitôt qu'il eut prononcé ces mots, un silence tomba.
english: As soon as he had spoken these words, silence fell.
tip: 'Eut prononcé' – passé antérieur of prononcer. Used after 'aussitôt que/dès que' in literary texts.

target: Rares sont les occasions de le rencontrer.
english: Opportunities to meet him are rare.
tip: 'Rares sont les occasions' fronts the adjective for emphasis, flipping verb and subject – literally 'rare are the chances.'

target: La manière dont il a réagi est inacceptable.
english: The way he reacted is unacceptable.
tip: 'Dont' replaces 'de': 'la manière dont il a réagi' = the way in which he reacted (réagir de cette manière).

target: Après qu'elle eut pleuré, elle se ressaisit.
english: After she had cried, she pulled herself together.
tip: 'Eut pleuré' is the literary past-in-the-past, standing in for 'avait pleuré' after après que. You'll meet it only in written narration.

target: Il a le beurre et l'argent du beurre.
english: He wants to have his cake and eat it too.
tip: Word for word this idiom is 'the butter and the money from the butter' – le beurre et l'argent du beurre. French says you can't keep the butter and pocket what you sold it for too.

target: Les biais méthodologiques ne sauraient être occultés.
english: Methodological biases cannot be concealed.
tip: Ne sauraient looks like 'would know', but savoir in the conditional means 'cannot' – a soft, formal impossibility: ne sauraient être occultés = these biases cannot be concealed.

target: Malgré la pluie, la cérémonie a eu lieu dehors.
english: Despite the rain, the ceremony took place outside.
tip: Events don't 'happen' in French, they 'have place' – avoir lieu. La cérémonie a eu lieu = the ceremony took place; there is no word for 'take' anywhere in it.

target: Il fit fortune dans le commerce des épices.
english: He made his fortune in the spice trade.
tip: French drops the 'his' here: it's faire fortune, not faire sa fortune. Il fit fortune = he made his fortune – the possessive lives only in the English.

target: Force est de constater que les résultats sont insuffisants.
english: We are forced to note that the results are insufficient.
tip: Force est de + infinitive: formal acknowledgment structure.

target: Cherchez la femme.
english: Look for the woman.
tip: 'Cherchez la femme' – 'look for the woman' – comes from Dumas: the notion that a woman is behind whatever tangle you're puzzling over.

target: Mieux vaut tard que jamais.
english: Better late than never.
tip: 'Mieux vaut' = it is better. Impersonal construction: 'mieux vaut tard que jamais'.

target: Qui se ressemble s'assemble.
english: Birds of a feather flock together.
tip: Literally 'those who resemble each other gather together' – and ressemble/assemble rhyme, which is why the proverb lodges in your head.

target: La question demeure entière.
english: The question remains unanswered.
tip: 'Demeure entière' is literally 'remains whole' – not one part of the question has been answered. Formal register.

target: L'habit ne fait pas le moine.
english: Clothes don't make the man.
tip: 'Habit' here is a false friend: French habit means a garment – the monk's robe – not a routine. Literally 'the robe doesn't make the monk.'

target: Nous nous garderons de toute généralisation hâtive.
english: We will refrain from any hasty generalization.
tip: 'Nous nous garderons de' is literally 'we'll guard ourselves from' – the reflexive turns 'guard' into 'refrain from.' Formal caution.

target: Les conclusions de cette recherche sont sans appel.
english: The conclusions of this research are unequivocal.
tip: 'Sans appel' = unequivocal/beyond dispute. Literally 'without appeal' (legal metaphor).

target: Force m'est de reconnaître que j'avais tort.
english: I am compelled to acknowledge that I was wrong.
tip: 'Force m'est de' means 'I'm compelled to' – literally 'force is upon me to,' where the m' marks who has no choice. Very formal.

target: Il serait prématuré de tirer des conclusions définitives.
english: It would be premature to draw definitive conclusions.
tip: That 'serait' (would be), not 'est' (is), softens the claim – French academic writing hedges with the conditional to sound less absolute.

target: Nous nous attacherons à démontrer la pertinence de cette approche.
english: We will endeavour to demonstrate the relevance of this approach.
tip: 'Nous nous attacherons à' is literally 'we'll attach ourselves to' demonstrating – the reflexive image means to commit to the task. Formal.

target: Cette approche permet de pallier les insuffisances des méthodes traditionnelles.
english: This approach makes it possible to remedy the shortcomings of traditional methods.
tip: 'Pallier' takes a direct object: 'pallier les insuffisances,' never 'pallier à' – unlike remédier à. Even native speakers slip on this one.

target: Qui vivra verra.
english: Time will tell.
tip: 'Qui vivra verra' – future tense in proverb. Literally: 'who will live will see'.

target: Vouloir, c'est pouvoir.
english: Where there's a will, there's a way.
tip: Literally 'To want is to be able.' French uses a bare infinitive as the subject – 'Vouloir' means 'wanting' – and 'c'est' bridges it to the second infinitive 'pouvoir.'

target: Les absents ont toujours tort.
english: The absent are always wrong.
tip: 'Ont toujours tort' – avoir tort is literally 'to have wrong.' French uses 'have,' not 'be,' for being at fault, and the absent always cop the blame.

target: Petit à petit, l'oiseau fait son nid.
english: Little by little, the bird builds its nest.
tip: 'Petit à petit' = 'little by little.' French doubles a word around à for a step-by-step feel: peu à peu, côte à côte, goutte à goutte.

target: Loin des yeux, loin du cœur.
english: Out of sight, out of mind.
tip: 'Loin des yeux, loin du cœur' is literally 'far from the eyes, far from the heart' – where English says 'out of sight, out of mind'.

target: Quoi qu'il en soit, la question reste ouverte.
english: Be that as it may, the question remains open.
tip: 'Quoi qu'il en soit' = be that as it may. Fixed expression: quoi que + subjunctive. Very formal.
